idiom_name: plain gateway class (PORO) with an injected connection object over Net::HTTP
implementation_notes: The idiomatic Ruby form - Fowler's own YouTube refactoring - is two plain objects: a connection class that owns the foreign call (Net::HTTP.start with Net::HTTP::Get, JSON parsing) and a gateway class that takes that connection in its constructor and exposes domestic methods returning hashes, Data.define or Struct values. Net::HTTP and JSON are standard library, so nothing has to be installed, and the connection can be swapped for a stub (minitest's stub or a hand-written double) in tests. For a relational resource the same shape is a thin gateway class over ActiveRecord or Sequel whose methods return domestic values, keeping the ORM's and the table's vocabulary out of callers.
code_sketch:
class YoutubeGateway                      # domestic vocabulary
  def initialize(connection) = (@connection = connection)   # injectable seam

  def item(id)
    record = @connection.list_videos([id]).fetch("items").first
    { views: record.dig("statistics", "viewCount").to_i,
      published: Date.parse(record.dig("snippet", "publishedAt")) }   # foreign -> domestic
  end
end
# connection (kept humble): YoutubeConnection.new.list_videos(ids) -> parsed Hash
pitfalls: Net::HTTP.start without the block form leaves the socket open: use the block (or ensure) so the connection is not left to the garbage collector.
Keep parsing out of the connection object - Fowler moves JSON.parse to the gateway precisely so the connection stays a humble object and a double can return canned payloads.
A bare rescue swallows errors the caller needs (Errno::ECONNREFUSED, Net::OpenTimeout, JSON::ParserError); translate them into one domestic error class explicitly.
Monkeypatching Net::HTTP globally in tests can leak into other examples; inject the connection instead.
